6 of 106 1. Introduction

(1) This document sets out the Council Tax Income Discount scheme, adopted by the Council, for working age applicants for the period from 1 April 2026. The scheme for persons who are pensioners is to be found in The Epsom & Ewell Borough Council (Council Tax Reduction Scheme) (Pensioners) 2026.

(2) This scheme may be cited as The Epsom & Ewell Borough Council (Council Tax Income Discount) (Working Age) 2026 and comes into effect on 1st April 2026.

(3) This scheme applies in relation to the billing authority in England known as Epsom & Ewell Borough Council and references in this scheme to “an authority” and “the authority” shall be to Epsom & Ewell Borough Council unless the context otherwise requires.

(4) This document details how the scheme operates for working age applicants and, in accordance with Section 13A of the Local Government Finance Act 1992, specifies the classes of person who are entitled to a discount under the scheme. To apply under this scheme an applicant must be the person who is liable to pay the Council Tax in respect of a dwelling, on any particular day, in accordance with Section 6 of the Local Government Finance Act 1992.

(5) The adopted scheme for working age applicants is an income banded scheme, which compares an applicant’s income and circumstances against a range of discounts available. The authority is required to specify a scheme for working age and therefore this scheme only applies to a person who: (a) has not attained the qualifying age for state pension credit; or (b) has attained the age for qualifying for state pension credit if he, and his partner, is a person on Income Support, on an Income Based Jobseeker’s Allowance, or an Income Related Employment and Support Allowance or on Universal Credit.

(6) The Council has determined that there will be one class of persons who will receive a discount in accordance with the adopted scheme. The scheme has qualifying criteria. In all cases the individuals must not be of a prescribed class exempted from receiving a discount as specified in Part 3 of this scheme.

1.1 Annual Review of Council Tax Reduction Scheme

For each financial year, the authority must consider whether to revise its scheme or to replace it with another scheme. The authority must make any revision to its scheme, or any replacement scheme, no later than 11 March in the financial year preceding that for which the revision or replacement scheme is to have effect.

Having given full consideration to the council tax reduction scheme from April 2020, and following an extensive public consultation, the authority has decided to implement a replacement scheme from 1 April 2021.

7 of 106 1.2 Replacement of Council Tax Support scheme from April 2021

1.2.1 Prescribed Statutory Requirements

The authority sets outs in Chapter 1, Parts 1 - 8, the statutory provisions that must apply to all applicants for a discount in accordance with the Prescribed Requirements Parts 1 to 3 and Schedules 7 to 8.

1.2.2 Local Scheme Requirements

Chapter 2 - Parts 9 to 19 and Schedules 1 to 3 set out the provisions of the Council Tax Reduction Schemes (Default Scheme) (England) Regulations 2012 (the “Default Scheme”), which the authority has adopted within its scheme.

1.3 Pensioners

The Government has said that local authorities must protect pensioners at the same level of support as the council tax benefit scheme and has prescribed a local scheme for pensioners with national rules.

This means that the authority has no discretion over the method or level of support provided to pensioners in accordance with the Prescribed Requirements, Parts 1 to 3, Schedules 1 to 6 and Schedules 7 to 8 where they apply to Pensioners.

This document therefore concentrates on the local Council Tax Income Discount scheme for persons who are not pensioners; the scheme for pensioners is to be found in The Epsom and Ewell Borough Council (Council Tax Reduction Scheme) (Pensioners) 2026.

1.4 Work Incentives

The authority’s scheme is required to meet the basic requirements of encouraging and incentivising work. The Government does not prescribe by regulation how the authority provides for work incentives in its scheme; it is for the authority to decide how best to provide work incentives for its individual communities.

1.5 Vulnerability

The Government does not prescribe by regulation which class of person(s) is deemed as vulnerable, it is for the authority to decide, having regard to its duties under the Acts referred to below.
